_about: Inputs to limitation_check. Every date names its official source. 'verified' means the date was read from that source's official PDF (hash in corpus/SOURCES.md); unverified dates must be checked before results depending on them are reported.

2017-18.source: CBIC Instruction 02/2021-22 (GST-Investigation), para 3: 05th & 07th February, 2020 (Notification no. 06/2020-Central Tax dated 03.02.2020); 07.02.2020 applies to some States, 05.02.2020 used here

2018-19.source: CBIC Instruction 02/2021-22 (GST-Investigation), para 3: 31st December, 2020 (Notification no. 80/2020-Central Tax dated 28.10.2020)

2019-20.source: CBIC Instruction 02/2021-22 (GST-Investigation), para 3: 31st March, 2021 (Notification no. 04/2021-Central Tax dated 28.02.2021)

2020-21.source: Notification no. 40/2021-Central Tax dated 29.12.2021 (inserts rule 80(1A)); official PDF not yet retrieved (cbic.gov.in TLS certificate failed); date taken from secondary reports. Statutory default would be 2021-12-31 (rule 80(1))

2021-22.source: CGST Rules r.80(1): on or before the thirty-first day of December following the end of the financial year (consolidation as amended to 01.01.2022); no extension notification checked

2022-23.source: CGST Rules r.80(1) default; no extension notification checked

2023-24.source: CGST Rules r.80(1) default; no extension notification checked

section_168A_order_extensions_s73._note: Extensions of the s.73(10) time limit for orders under s.73(9) (tax not paid / short paid / ITC wrongly availed). The latest notification for a year wins. They do not apply to s.74. Their validity is challenged before several High Courts and the Supreme Court (SLP 4240/2025), so any answer that depends on them is contested.
